summary: Context menu is rendered as a portal/popover anchored to the message on React but appears as an inline stacked block below the message on Android, causing large layout drift.
Android menu has 7 items including a 'Select Text' entry plus an extra 'Follow Thread' on React that becomes its own grouped section; React shows 7 items with 'Select Message' and no 'Select Text'.

React groups emoji reactions inside the popover and places Copy Link/Copy Markdown/Select Message in one block, then Open Thread/Save Message/Follow Thread in another; Android splits Copy Link/Copy Markdown/Select Text/Select Message into a single block and Open Thread/Save Message into another, with Convert to Task isolated.
React's menu is narrower (icon rail ~32px, total width ~280px) while Android's menu is wider (~360px) and uses larger row heights and padding.

Section dividers are thick black bars on React but appear as hairline 1px rules on Android, and React uses bolder/larger label typography (≈16px/600) versus Android's lighter/smaller labels (≈14px/regular).
likelyCauses: Android Compose implementation re-implemented the menu as a stacked column of cards rather than as a single floating popover anchored to the message bubble.
Menu item list source-of-truth differs between platforms (React uses thread-message-menu config; Android reads a different menu definition that includes 'Select Text' and omits 'Follow Thread').
Different component primitive used on Android (Card/OutlinedButton rows vs. React's Menu/Popover), producing mismatched paddings, dividers, and font metrics.
Token mismatch for spacing/radius/elevation between design system web and Compose themes.
analysis.suggestedOwner: Android platform team (message thread surface) with design-system parity review

Normalize row height, horizontal padding, and font size/weight to the React values; replace thick black dividers with 1px hairline dividers.
Use a single token for popover width (~280px) instead of stretching to the message column width.
Verify icon size and emoji reaction glyph scaling so the Android reactions row matches React's ~20px icons.
intentional: Difference in message content (#product hash suffix) and timestamp is test-fixture data, not a UI bug.

cases.title: Thread Forward Modal

summary: Modal positioning: React baseline has a narrow bottom-sheet style modal at left while Android renders a wider centered modal covering most of the viewport.

Subtitle content differs: React reads '2 selected from #design' while Android reads '2 selected' (omits source channel).

Target selection UI is structurally different: React shows a flat scrollable list of selectable targets (@artin, @Cindy, #android-artifacts) above the message preview; Android shows a 'Destinations' list with avatars, subtitles, and a checkmark on the selected #design row.

Designer delivered two separate specs (web vs Android) instead of sharing the forward-modal source-of-truth component.

Restore 'FORWARD' uppercase bold header and '2 selected from #design' subtitle text.

Audit Kuikly Button and TextInput spacing tokens on iOS to match Android dp values for horizontal padding and inter-button gap.

summary: Android cards render with noticeably larger vertical spacing (more padding/margin) than React cards, pushing content lower and increasing the gap before 'Load More'.
Relative timestamps differ: React shows '17/17/18 days ago' while Android shows '14/14/15 days ago' on the three cards.
Header subtitle weight differs: React's '5 saved' appears in a lighter/thinner monospace style; Android's '5 saved' is rendered in a standard, slightly bolder sans-serif weight.
Third card avatar differs: React shows a solid cyan/blue square placeholder, Android shows a building/emoji-style icon glyph.
Third card author label wraps to two lines ('Product UX Designer') on React but is rendered inline/compact on Android, causing different text layout in the meta row.

Android uses default Material typography/weights while React uses a custom lighter monospace font for the header subtitle.
Android Card component applies larger default content padding than the React card implementation.
Avatar asset mapping for the 'Product UX Designer' author is missing on Android, falling back to a generic building glyph instead of the colored square.

Align relative-time formatter so both clients render the same 'N days ago' value.
Use the same subtitle font-weight and family on Android as React for the '5 saved' count.
Fix the avatar fallback so the third card shows the same cyan square placeholder on Android.
Ensure the author display name uses a consistent layout (wrap vs. single-line) across platforms.

summary: Bookmark icon in the top-right of each saved result card differs: React shows a filled bookmark glyph, iOS shows a circular info (i) icon.
Timestamp text differs across cards: React shows '17 days ago', '17 days ago', '18 days ago'; iOS shows '14 days ago', '14 days ago', '15 days ago' — off by ~3 days.
Date text in iOS header reads '1170×2532' instead of a human-readable date like React's '1026×1800'.
Second card metadata layout differs: React wraps '17 days' / 'ago' onto two lines with a gap between 'artin' and the timestamp; iOS keeps timestamp on one line and tucks it closer to the author name.
Third card avatar differs: React shows a solid cyan square; iOS shows a grid/dotted square pattern.
likelyCauses: iOS build is rendering an info (i) SF Symbol in place of the bookmark icon used by the React/web component.
iOS and React are pulling timestamps from different sources/formatters or using different relative-time rounding.
iOS layout uses a different flex/auto-layout strategy, causing metadata row wrapping and larger card heights.
Avatar component on iOS falls back to a placeholder pattern instead of the solid color swatch used on web.
iOS viewport includes safe-area/home-indicator regions not present in the web baseline canvas.
suggestedFixes: Verify the iOS saved-results card uses the bookmark SF Symbol (bookmark.fill) matching the web bookmark glyph, not the info.circle icon.
Align relative-time formatting and source between React and iOS so day counts match (or freeze timestamps in test fixtures).
Normalize the metadata row layout (author + timestamp on a single line with consistent spacing) across platforms.
Ensure the avatar component renders the same swatch/pattern on iOS as on web, or use a shared placeholder spec.
Add safe-area/home-indicator insets to the React baseline or crop the iOS screenshot to the same component bounds before comparison.
intentional: Different canvas dimensions (342×620 vs 1170×2532) are expected between web and iOS baselines.
Platform tag text difference ('REACT' vs 'IOS') is expected.

summary: Action icon in top-right of each saved card differs: Android shows a bookmark/save glyph, iOS shows an info/info-circle (ⓘ) glyph — semantic/icon mismatch.

iOS canvas is significantly taller than Android (1170×2532 vs 342×620), producing large empty whitespace below the 'Load More' button on iOS; the iOS layout is not vertically constrained to the component bounds.
Card chrome, typography, spacing, and divider are visually isomorphic between the two sides aside from the action icon swap.
Metadata badge top-right: Android label 'ANDROID' vs iOS label 'IOS' — expected/intentional platform label, not a defect.
Pixel mismatch ratio 5.71% concentrated in the action-icon region and the empty iOS lower canvas.
likelyCauses: Platform-specific icon resource mapping: the saved-card trailing action is being resolved from different icon sets per platform (bookmark vs info).
Missing component-bounds crop on iOS side (crop.current is null) so iOS is compared against its full 2532px canvas instead of a clipped component region equal to the Android crop.
No fixed vertical container height on the page on iOS, so content sits at the top and leaves large empty space; Android was cropped to component bounds which masks this.
suggestedFixes: Unify the trailing action icon across Android and iOS: pin to a single semantic icon (e.g., bookmark) via a shared Kuikly asset, or branch the icon by intent (save vs info) explicitly and keep parity.
Crop the iOS canvas to the same component-bounds rect used on Android before running the pixel-perfect diff so whitespace is not counted as mismatch.
Constrain the page content area to a fixed height (or center vertically) so both platforms render an equal-sized component footprint.
Add a Slock tolerance rule to ignore the platform badge label ('ANDROID'/'IOS') when comparing.
Re-run the visual test after fixes; target pixelMismatchRatio < 1% and pixelPerfectSimilarity > 0.99.
intentional: Platform label badge in top-right of the canvas reads 'ANDROID' on the left and 'IOS' on the right by design.

summary: Timestamp text differs: React shows '17 days ago'/'20 days ago'/'20 days ago' while Android shows '14 days ago'/'16 days ago'/'16 days ago' — likely a data snapshot/fixture mismatch, not a styling issue.
Spacing between the tab row ('All / Unread / Mentions') and 'Mark all read' button is tighter on Android; the filter row sits closer to the dividing line on the right side.
Vertical spacing between activity cards is larger on Android, causing the list to start lower and end with more empty space at the bottom.
The '@Cindy' card body text on Android uses a smaller font size and appears more compact, while React renders the Chinese characters at a noticeably larger weight.
Tab buttons ('All','Unread','Mentions') appear slightly narrower on Android with reduced internal horizontal padding, making the yellow 'All' chip smaller.
likelyCauses: Activity card timestamp rendered from different fixture snapshots between platforms
Android Compose implementation using different list item padding/density defaults than the React baseline
Android theming overrides tab control min-height and chip padding
Font scaling/sp values on Android diverge from React's rem/px sizing for card body text
suggestedFixes: Align the activity feed fixture so both platforms render identical relative timestamps (or freeze a deterministic date).
Match Android card vertical spacing to the React values (increase outer card padding or row gap to match the ~28px React rhythm).
Adjust Android tab/chip dimensions (minHeight, horizontal padding) to match React baseline widths.
Reconcile font sizes for card body content (e.g., the 'Cindy:' line) so Android scales match React's text-sm/lg tokens.
Verify the bottom whitespace — if intentional, mark as accepted variance; if not, tighten card padding or reduce inter-card gap on Android.
intentional: Different absolute 'days ago' values likely intentional if using a live data source, but should be normalized for visual regression baselines

cases.title: Tasks Panel States

summary: Android header shows a square checkbox icon to the left of the 'Tasks' title; React header has no icon.

Task card vertical density is higher on Android — all four status sections (TODO, IN PROGRESS, IN REVIEW, DONE) fit on one canvas, while React scrolls with more spacing per card and crops the last card's status badge.
React card bodies have noticeably more vertical padding between the metadata row and the title; Android cards are more compact.
React's TODO column count badge ('1') sits further right of the orange TODO pill with a wider gap; Android uses a tighter inline spacing.
likelyCauses: Android header component renders a leading checkbox/list icon by default that React's header omits.
Android task card uses a denser spacing scale (smaller vertical paddings) than React's card spacing tokens.
React list may apply extra section header height or larger card min-height from a different layout primitive.
suggestedFixes: Decide whether the header checkbox icon should be shared; if yes, add it to React's Tasks header; if platform-only, document as intentional.
Align task card vertical padding and section spacing between Android and React using the shared spacing tokens.
Normalize the column header (pill + count) inline gap to the same value across platforms.
If the React panel is intentionally scrollable at this height, ensure the card density matches so content fits comparably or confirm intentional density difference.
intentional: Android task card top-right timestamp (relative format) — react-adopts-later per artin 2026-07-06.
Android task card bottom-left assignee line ('Unassigned' / '@name') — react-adopts-later per artin 2026-07-06.

summary: Android (right) adds a 'Preferred Language' section with a dropdown (showing 'English') and a Save button, which is missing in React (left).

likelyCauses: Feature drift between web and Android builds — Preferred Language and Manual translation mode were added on Android but not in the React component.

cases.title: Settings Notifications Page

summary: React shows a single 'PUSH NOTIFICATIONS' section with web-push explanation, 'UNAVAILABLE' status, 'Enable Push Notifications' CTA (pink/disabled), and 'Mute this server' with checkbox + Save button.

Android shows a materially different, OS-level notifications control surface: 'Notification permission / Allowed' panel, 'Enabled/Disabled' toggle, 'Keep alive / Normal' toggle, 'Manage notifications' deep link, 'Test notification / Ready' panel, and 'Workspace mute / Unmuted/Muted' toggle.
React layout is compact (~half the viewport) and padded at top; Android layout fills more vertical space with multiple stacked cards/groups.
Header row (back arrow + 'Notifications' title + divider) is visually consistent across both sides.
React uses a muted/disabled pink button affordance for 'Enable Push Notifications' and 'Save'; Android uses yellow-highlighted button states with outlined (filled white) buttons for primary actions.
likelyCauses: React (web) uses Web Push API which is unavailable in the test browser, so the page renders the web-push fallback state with 'UNAVAILABLE' banner and disabled CTA.

Android uses platform-native APIs (NotificationManager, foreground services, system channels) and exposes OS-level controls (permission panel, tray notifications, keep-alive, manage-in-system, workspace mute) that don't exist on web.
The same Settings page is implemented as two separate platform-specific surfaces rather than a single cross-platform component, leading to divergent copy and control sets.
Crop mismatch (component-bounds vs viewport-bounds) inflates pixel mismatch beyond what is caused by UI alone.
analysis.suggestedOwner: Platform notifications / settings feature owner (mobile + web)
suggestedFixes: Confirm whether the divergence is intentional: if Android should expose OS-level settings (permission, tray, keep-alive, manage, test, workspace mute) and web should expose web-push equivalents, mark the page as platform-acceptable and adjust tolerances or comparison contract accordingly.
Normalize crop contracts: switch both sides to viewport-bounds (or both to component-bounds) so Slock isn't comparing an element-cropped React frame against a full-frame Android shot.
Add a shared spec for the Notifications page that lists required controls per platform; if a control only exists on one platform, document it in component metadata so visual tests don't flag it.

On the web side, redesign the 'PUSH NOTIFICATIONS' empty/unavailable state to still match the card/divider structure used on Android (e.g., outlined cards with consistent padding) so layout pattern is comparable.
Ensure disabled-button styling is consistent: React uses pink/disabled whereas Android uses yellow-outlined — align the design tokens for 'primary disabled' across platforms.

Android 'Notification permission / Allowed' panel and 'Manage notifications' deep link are OS-level affordances unique to mobile.
Android 'Keep alive / Normal' toggle corresponds to a foreground service behavior that does not exist on web.
'Workspace mute / Unmuted / Muted' on Android is a native mute affordance and may not have an exact web equivalent.

cases.title: Settings Connected Apps Page

summary: Different layout density: Android uses a more compact, stacked layout with merged/shorter section headers, while React uses larger, separated cards with more whitespace.

Section header style differs: React shows 'CONNECTED APPS' and 'BUILT-IN' as small uppercase labels in muted color above cards; Android replaces these with inline section icons and titles ('Connected Apps', 'Built-in') plus subtitle text under the page title.

Counter/pill representation differs: React renders 'Marketplace 3 / Installed 2 / My apps 1' as combined labeled pills; Android splits these into separate numeric tiles ('3', '2', '1') with labels beneath, then a secondary row of icon-prefixed tabs.

App card action button variant differs: React 'Open' button is solid pink with no icon; Android 'Open' button adds an external-link icon next to the label. 'Install' (React) vs 'Details' (Android) labels differ for the same card slot.

Iconography and typography weight: Android uses outlined leading icons (link, store, check, key) and lighter body type for descriptions; React uses plain bordered tiles with bold titles and no leading icons.
likelyCauses: Different component libraries / design-system implementations between web (React) and native (Android) targets producing divergent visual defaults.
Independent re-implementation of the Connected Apps page in Android rather than shared design tokens, leading to restructured information hierarchy.
Varied interpretation of spec for counter/pill groupings and section labeling.
suggestedFixes: Define and share a single visual contract (tokens) for section labels, counter pills, and card actions across React and Android implementations.
Unify header treatment: decide whether a subtitle under 'Connected Apps' belongs in both platforms and render consistently.
Standardize the numeric counters (Marketplace/Installed/My apps) — either as combined pills (React) or as numeric tiles (Android) — and apply the chosen pattern everywhere.
Align action buttons on app cards: same label semantics ('Open' vs 'Details' vs 'Install') and same icon usage across platforms.
Match search input styling: include or omit the leading search icon consistently and unify placeholder text casing/ellipsis.
intentional: Platform-native density conventions may justify the more compact Android layout and added icons.
Counter pattern difference could be an intentional adaptation to narrow-viewport information density.

summary: Layout is vertically split into two independent cards on iOS (Third-party apps and Built-in) while React places them stacked with a shared 'Available to all Raft users' context.
iOS introduces extra in-card stat tiles (3 Marketplace, 2 Installed, 1 My apps) inside the Third-party card, plus an 'EXPERIMENTAL' badge that is not shown in that card on React.
Tab order on iOS is rearranged: icon-prefixed tabs (Marketplace / Installed / My) appear below the stat tiles, whereas React renders a single 'CONNECTED APPS' label above the card.
'Marketplace 3' / 'Installed 2' / 'My apps 1' chip style on React becomes large numeric tiles with truncated label ('Marketplac…') on iOS — text is clipped.

iOS loses the green 'BUILT-IN' pill on the GitHub row, replaces descriptive text with a list ('Available to all users & agents · Built-in source control integration · github.com'), and changes the action label from 'Open' to 'Open' with an external-link icon.
likelyCauses: React and iOS implementations were built from different design specs; iOS port appears to follow a card-based refactor not back-applied to web.
Stat-count tiles and tab bar were introduced on iOS without an equivalent update on React.
iOS component library renders icons by default (marketplace/installed/key, external-link, eye) where React uses text-only badges.
Truncation on 'Marketplace' tile caused by insufficient fixed width / lack of Text ellipsis handling.
Missing 'BUILT-IN' and 'PRODUCTIVILITY' tags on iOS suggest tag/badge component was not ported or was conditionally suppressed.
suggestedFixes: Align the page structure between web and iOS: pick either stacked sections or split cards and apply consistently.
Add the missing tags/badges on iOS: green 'BUILT-IN' pill on GitHub row, yellow 'PRODUCTIVITY' tag on Slack Bridge row, and the 'CONNECTED APPS' / 'EXPERIMENTAL' labels in their React positions.
Decide on tab style parity: if React uses chip-style counters, render them as chips on iOS; if numeric tiles are desired on iOS, ensure label width allows full text or add ellipsis tooltip.
Restore React's descriptive sub-header under 'Connected Apps' on iOS, or remove it on both.
Match CTA variants: use the same primary pink 'Open' / 'Install' buttons (no external-link or eye icon) on iOS, or update React to match the new iconography.

summary: Truncated third-party app card: on Android the title reads 'Third-party apps for this server' (two short lines) while on iOS it reads 'Third-party apps for' / 'this server' (a slightly earlier line break).
Experimental stats tile 'Marketplace' label is truncated to 'Marketplac' on iOS (missing trailing 'e') versus full 'Marketpla…' ellipsis truncation on Android.
Tab pill set differs in label width and ellipsis: Android shows 'My A… 1' while iOS shows 'My 1' — iOS drops the 'apps' word with no ellipsis, indicating a width/policy divergence in the tab.
GitHub built-in card extends further on iOS: includes the extra url line 'github.com' rendered as a separate line below the description, whereas Android merges/inlines it inside the description text.

Slack Bridge description line breaks differently: Android ends with 'channel / metadata' on three wrapped lines starting from 'Messages and channel'; iOS breaks it as 'channel / metadata' with 'Messages and channel' on one line and 'metadata' on the next — slightly tighter wrap.
likelyCauses: Non-uniform text-wrapping/line-break rules between Kuikly Android and iOS text engines (e.g., different handling of maxLines + ellipsize).
Tab/segmented control uses fixed min width per platform, causing 'My apps' label to overflow on iOS but get ellipsized on Android.
iOS renders longer URLs or descriptions outside the constrained description maxLines, while Android collapses them.
Inconsistent horizontal padding scale factor between Android and iOS for Card and StatTile components.
iOS home-indicator safe area / scroll-edge affordance overlaps the last Details button, while Android does not display this gesture indicator.
suggestedFixes: Normalize text wrapping: apply a unified ellipsize + maxLines policy (e.g., maxLines=2, ellipsize=end) for the 'Third-party apps' title and for the Marketplace stat tile label.
Widen the stat tiles' content padding or reduce label font size so 'Marketplace' renders in full on iOS; mirror the Android truncation only at narrower breakpoints.
Audit tab pill min width / label strategy: either allow 'My apps' to wrap, shrink icon+badge region, or auto-fit by reducing tab count padding so the label displays identically on both OSes.
Move the 'github.com' link to a dedicated metadata line on both platforms (consistent slot), not as inline text inside the description body.
Reconcile horizontal padding: share Card/Section spacing tokens across Android and iOS (apply same dp scale at 1170×2532 vs 390×844).

cases.title: Members Agent Detail Profile Screen

summary: Android header avatar is rendered as a pixel-art/QR-like placeholder while React uses a solid cyan square.

Android top nav Message button label truncated to 'Mess...' while React shows full 'Message'.
Android Activity tab label truncated to 'Activi...' while React shows full 'Activity'.
Android header shows a trailing folder/file icon after Reminders that React does not.

Android avatar component is unstyled or default loading placeholder; React uses a solid color fallback.
Android Info section uses a grid layout with two columns while React uses a single-column definition list, causing the Computer/Created/Creator rewrap.
Android renders role as a colored 'Member' badge with edit affordance; React renders an outlined 'No role' pill, indicating different default role data or component version.
Mismatch in Created date suggests test fixture divergence rather than UI bug.

Apply consistent header truncation (max-width + ellipsis) on Android for title, description, and tab labels.

cases.title: Thread Message Row Long Inline Code

summary: Avatar and timestamp row layout differs: React shows avatar at far left with a clear gap before 'Cindy' name and a truncated 'Keeps vis… 06/25 05:55 AM' subtitle; Android shows the avatar inline at left with a single-line subtitle 'Keeps visual testing … 06/25 05:55' that extends further right.

Body text wraps to different column widths: React renders at a wider body width so long inline-code paths wrap on fewer, longer lines; Android renders at a noticeably narrower effective text width, causing more frequent line breaks in the long path and the gradlew command blocks.

Long inline-code spans break at different points: React keeps the path and command as a single continuous yellow box wrapping at the container edge; Android splits the yellow fill into separate adjacent boxes (visible gap/border between segments such as 'raft.build.markdown' and '.inlineCode', and between 'owner-key' and '-consumes-thread-route'), producing a visually segmented wrap.

The bottom gradlew command block is clipped/cropped on Android — the final line 'visual.KmpVisualScreenshotCapture' is cut off at the canvas bottom (390×844), whereas on React the same content fits within bounds (final visible line is '.captureThreadMessageRowLongInlineCode.').
Right-side metadata badge uses different casing/label: 'REACT' (green) on the left vs 'ANDROID' (yellow) on the right — expected but worth noting for test screenshot consistency.
likelyCauses: Android markdown/inline-code renderer treats each visual line of a wrapped code span as a separate background-painted box rather than a single rounded background that flows across line breaks.
Android text container width is smaller (different horizontal padding or avatar/text-column geometry) causing the long code blocks to wrap at shorter line lengths.
Canvas height (844pt) is insufficient for the Android layout's taller line count, resulting in bottom-edge clipping of the last gradlew command line.
suggestedFixes: Make Android paint a single continuous yellow code-span background across wrapped lines (or merge adjacent code-span backgrounds) so wrapped paths look like one chip like React.
Reconcile avatar/text-column padding on Android to match React's body width, or reduce body horizontal insets so long inline code has more room before wrapping.
Extend test canvas height or shorten fixture content so the final gradlew command line is not clipped on Android; alternatively cap content to fit 844pt on both platforms.
Verify the metadata badge color/label scheme (REACT green / ANDROID yellow) is intentional and consistent across visual-test baselines.
intentional: @KMP-专家 is rendered as an underlined @mention chip on Android but as plain text on React — intentional platform difference (Android tags all @mentions regardless of resolution).
Bare #520 is rendered as a yellow task chip on Android and as plain text on React — intentional platform difference (Android tags all bare #number task refs).
Mention @artin and the #markdown专修 channel chip are tagged on both sides since they resolve to known entities — this is the intended shared behavior.

summary: Inline code spans render at a slightly different base size/leading on iOS causing the long-path block to overflow the canvas at the right edge (last few characters clipped) and the gradlew command to wrap onto an extra line.
Long inline code blocks on iOS appear to render in a slightly heavier weight and the yellow frame extends edge-to-edge, differing from the React baseline which has visible right-margin.

On iOS the rightmost portion of long inline-code lines (e.g., '…identity-…', '…KmpVisualScreenshot…', '…MessageRowLongInlineCode') is clipped/cropped at the canvas right edge, whereas React wraps cleanly within bounds.
Tag chip widths (#markdown专修, #markdown专修:692d9e88, @artin, #42, #43) measure slightly wider on iOS, pushing subsequent tokens onto different line breaks vs. React.

Header meta row (Keeps vis… vs Keeps visual testing 06/25 05:55) truncates differently: React shows ellipsis-cropped 'vis…' with timestamp on a new horizontal segment, iOS keeps the channel name fully but still aligns timestamp on the same row with different spacing.
likelyCauses: iOS WebView/text engine uses a different monospace font metrics than React, so each inline-code span occupies more horizontal space and the existing max-width/word-break CSS does not constrain it the same way.
Right padding or available content width on the iOS message row is smaller relative to text size, so long unbreakable tokens exceed the row and get clipped rather than wrapping.
Inline-code chip styling (yellow background + border) is applied at a slightly larger padding/font-size on iOS, expanding chip width.
Differences in how bold and CN glyphs are rendered across platforms shift line-break points, cascading into different wrap positions for long inline codes.
suggestedFixes: Normalize monospace font-family and font-size for inline code spans across platforms so measured widths match.
Reduce inline-code horizontal padding or add a small right-margin so long paths render fully within row bounds on iOS.
Ensure the message row's content area width and right padding are consistent with React; add overflow-wrap/word-break rules for long unbreakable tokens.
Tighten header meta truncation rules so the channel-name + timestamp layout produces identical ellipsis behavior on both platforms.
Verify the yellow-fill code-chip background does not extend to the canvas edge on iOS by adding a max-width or inset consistent with React.

#520 appears as a plain task chip on iOS and as plain text on React - same intentional platform-difference noted in metadata (#416, artin keep-android-style).
#markdown专修 renders with the resolved-channel pink/blue split chip styling on iOS for both occurrences, while React only styles the known one - intentional divergence, not a defect.

summary: Inline code spans clip the right edge of the message bubble on iOS; long paths and command spans are truncated mid-character (e.g. 'msg-i', 'receipt/owner-key-con', 'without-sourc', 'fallback/max-wi', 'gamma-del', 'kapp', 'KmpVisu').
Android wraps long inline code/command spans onto additional lines within the bubble; iOS does not wrap and instead overflows horizontally past the available width.
Code/command chip yellow fill and black frame render at noticeably different widths: iOS chips extend further than the text content, with the frame not hugging the wrapped lines.
Long-path code block on iOS loses visible trailing characters ('pa-lambda-mu.' cut off) while Android shows the full path on its own line.
Command block content on iOS is cut off after 'captureThre' / 'adMessageRowLongInlineCode', while Android shows the full command text wrapping into multiple lines.
likelyCauses: iOS TextKit / CoreText layout does not break inside long no-break tokens the way Android's StaticLayout does, causing inline code and paths to overflow instead of wrap.
Missing NSLineBreakStrategy / lineBreakStrategy / allowsBreakingTightLineBreaks on the TextView/Text component used for markdown rendering on iOS.
Inline code (yellow chip) container has no max-width / flexible width constraint on iOS, so its background rect is sized to the raw (non-wrapped) string and clips at the message width.
Possible width/inset mismatch: iOS may be using a fixed pixel width for the message bubble without accounting for font metric differences, leaving less room for wrap than Android's dp-based layout.
suggestedFixes: Enable line-break inside long tokens on iOS (e.g. lineBreakStrategy(.standard) / .hangulWordPriorityStyle / allowsBreakingTightLineBreaks=true) for the markdown body and inline-code text views.
Give inline-code and command chips a flexible width (match parent / maxWidth of bubble minus padding) so they wrap rather than overflow; let the yellow+black frame size to the wrapped content.
Verify message bubble inner padding/width on iOS matches Android's dp-equivalent so chips and paths share the same available text width.
Normalize wrap behavior between Android and iOS for tag chips (#42, #43, #markdown专修:692d9e88) so unknown chips don't push tokens onto a new line.
Re-run the fixture after fixes; the 'Long path should wrap inline without ellipsis' and 'Command should wrap with the same yellow fill and black frame' cases are the primary acceptance checks.
intentional: @KMP-专家 and bare '#520' are rendered as styled mention/underline on Android and as plain text on iOS — platform-difference (Android tags everything, iOS gates on known entities); both behaviors are correct for their platform.
Bare '#markdown专修' channel and '#markdown专修:692d9e88' task/thread chips appear styled on Android and plain on iOS for the same known-entity reason; intentional per artin's '全部 tag 呗' ruling.

cases.title: Settings Administration Full Height Screen

summary: Android renders the Administration settings screen in a single scrollable form whereas React presents settings as discrete card-based sections, causing large vertical/structural differences (~31px taller on Android).

Header pattern differs: Android shows a back arrow + 'Administration' page title; React uses a small caption 'Settings: Administration Full-Height Screen' at the top of each card with no global title.

Owners & Admins control differs: React uses an 'Add owner/admin' select + 'Admin' select + 'Update Role' button + member list card; Android uses a single 'Control who can manage this workspace' card listing one owner with a 'Last owner' pill and no role-update UI.

System Channels differs: React has an interactive 'Hide #all channel' toggle with Save button and descriptive copy; Android shows a read-only 'System Channels' card with an 'Unavailable' status and eye icon.
Pending Invites differs: React displays invites as compact rows with a date and small X icon; Android expands each invite into a full card showing inviter email and a large 'Revoke' button.
likelyCauses: Android implementation reimplemented the Administration form as a new card-based layout instead of reusing the React component contract (different component library / native form widgets).
Different form patterns: Android uses radio groups, segmented controls, and inline cards; React uses selects, checkboxes, and inline label/input rows.
Save-button semantics differ: React uses per-section Save buttons with default disabled state; Android uses always-enabled filled buttons with leading icons.
Additional sections (Sidebar Order, Danger Zone) were added on Android but not part of the React baseline contract used for this snapshot.
Toggle/pill style: Android uses yellow-filled 'Required' pill and radio highlight; React uses simple checkbox toggles.
suggestedFixes: Reuse the React baseline contract for section structure and labels (e.g., 'Hide #all channel' toggle, 'Enable message translation', 'Hide human directory'), or update the baseline to match the new Android design and re-baseline.
Normalize Save/Update buttons: same color, same enabled-by-default behavior, same iconography, and same placement across both platforms.
Unify Onboarding control: pick either a select (React) or a radio list (Android) and apply consistently; align New Agent Greeting control (select vs segmented Yes/No).
Unify Pre-Join Agreement: choose inline title/body/preview (React) or stacked cards with character counter (Android) and apply on both.
Remove or include 'Sidebar Order' and 'Danger Zone' consistently across platforms; if platform-specific, exclude from full-height visual contract.
intentional: Sidebar Order card showing 'Unavailable' status on Android.
Danger Zone with 'Delete Server' being Android-only.

summary: Header structure differs: React uses 'CONNECTED APPS' label with link icon on the left; Android uses a back arrow plus 'Connected Apps' title bar with a separate breadcrumb row beneath.
Experimental tag placement differs: React shows it in the header near the title; Android shows it inside the description card below the body text.

'Register app' button position and shape differ: React shows it inline in the header area; Android places it floating to the right of the 'Third-party apps for this server' heading, partially overlapping the card edge.

Tab layout inverts: React shows pill-style tabs (Marketplace 3, Installed 2, My apps 1) inside the description card; Android shows them as separate navigation tabs/icons (Marketplace, Installed, My Apps) below the card, then duplicates the stat tiles inside the card.
Section icons missing in React: Android adds a package icon next to 'Built-in' and a storefront icon next to 'Marketplace' that do not exist on the React side.
likelyCauses: Independent redesign of the Connected Apps page in the Android app rather than parity with the React baseline.
Different design system tokens (spacing, radius, typography weight) applied across platforms.
Component-level divergence: avatar tiles, status pills, and category badges not implemented in the Android variant.
